title: Keep the gateway fast when header names collide

blocks.text: The API gateway keeps each request's headers in a `HashMap<HeaderName, String>`. Last night a client sent requests with a few thousand made-up header names, all with the same `hashCode()`, and every gateway node spent its CPU in `HeaderName.equals`. The debug log, which lists a request's header names from a `TreeSet<HeaderName>`, has never worked either: it fails with a `ClassCastException`.

`HeaderName` must keep its `equals` and `hashCode`: names are the same header only when they are spelled exactly alike, and other services rely on the hash. Finish the `TODO` in `src/main/java/practice/HeaderName.java` (the method and whatever the class needs for it to be used).

When you're done, the debug log's set works, a lookup among thousands of names that share one hash code costs a few dozen `equals` calls rather than thousands, and names that differ only in case stay two headers in the sorted log. About two lines in total. The tests count calls through `HeaderName.EQUALS_CALLS`.

cases.says: a HashMap keyed by HeaderName finds every stored header, and a TreeSet of names holds each of them
with 4,096 names sharing one hash code, a lookup calls equals only a few dozen times at most
names that differ only in case are two different headers in a sorted set, as they are in equals

origin.section: Colliding HashMap Keys Stay Fast Only When They Are Comparable

concepts: HashMap turns a crowded bin into a tree ordered by hash and then by compareTo, so colliding keys stay cheap to look up only when their class is Comparable of itself with an order that separates unequal keys.
